name: What If Unstable Soil Is Found During Excavation?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a retaining wall contractor finds unstable soil during construction?
mainEntity.text: What happens if a retaining wall contractor finds unstable soil during construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unstable soil is a common reason retaining wall projects change once excavation begins. The contractor may need to undercut weak material, replace it with compacted engineered fill, adjust the footing depth or width, add reinforcement, or pause work until an engineer reviews the condition. Continuing without correction can compromise the wall’s performance and increase the risk of settlement or movement later. In Los Angeles County, site soil can vary dramatically even within the same property, especially on hillsides or older lots with fill. A contractor should explain what testing or inspection was done and how they handle unexpected soil conditions. If unstable soil is discovered, the goal is not to move faster but to rebuild the design around the actual site conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: If unstable soil is found, the contractor may need to widen the footing, remove weak material, add engineered fill, change the wall design, or stop work until the site is re-evaluated. This can affect cost and schedule. The safest response is to recheck the design before continuing rather than building on questionable soil.
